narrative: This collection agency calls me 4 to 5 times a day, sometimes before 8am, about a payday loan debt. I have asked them multiple times to only contact me by mail and they keep calling anyway. It's gotten to the point where I'm afraid to answer my phone.
extracted_allegations: Collection agency calls 4 to 5 times a day about a payday loan debt | Some calls occur before 8am | Customer asked multiple times to be contacted only by mail and the agency continues to call
policy_cited: 08 General Dispute Handling Process (Standard process step 4, and 'What counts as a complete response'); drafted in line with Policy 10 (Prohibited Language) and Policy 11 (Response Tone and Format)
draft_text:
You told us that a collection agency has been calling you four to five times a day about a payday loan debt, that some calls come before 8am, and that the calls have continued even though you've asked to be contacted by mail only. We understand how frustrating that has been.

Here is what we found for each point you raised.

1. Number of calls: Our call records show 4 calls on March 30 and 5 calls on March 31, which matches what you described. There was also a call on April 1 at 12:05 that was answered and lasted about 2 minutes.

2. Calls before 8am: Our records confirm two calls before 8am. They were placed at 7:41am on March 30 and 7:55am on March 31.

3. Your requests for mail-only contact: We did not find a mail-only request in your account notes or history. The only mailed notice we have on record is dated March 2, before the calls began. Requests made by phone or directly to the agency may not appear in our records, so we can't confirm whether those requests were made or whether calls continued after them.

Outcome: The call frequency and the early-morning calls are confirmed. No change has been made to how you are contacted, because there is no mail-only request on record. We have not reached a finding on whether calls continued after you asked for mail-only contact.

Next steps: Please reply to this message or call us at the number on your account to confirm that you want contact by mail only. If you can, tell us when and how you made your earlier requests, who you spoke with, and the dates of any calls since. We will review whatever you send. You are welcome to send more information at any time.

Our records show your payment of $118.75 was received through the mobile app on April 13th, one day before your April 14th due date. The payment didn't post to your account until April 15th, and the $35 late fee was assessed that same day. Our records confirm the payment was on time and that the late fee was applied in error. You don't need to send your screenshot, since our own records already show the April 13th payment.

We've referred the correction of this fee for approval. We'll update you once a decision has been made, and we can't confirm the outcome until then.

If you have anything else you'd like us to look at, please send it at any time and we'll review it. You're also free to raise this through any other channel you choose. For any further correspondence, please quote case reference 21633667.

narrative: I set up autopay for this loan six months ago and it worked fine until last month, when my payment was never withdrawn and I was charged a late fee as a result. I have a screenshot of my autopay settings still showing as active.
extracted_allegations: Autopay payment was never withdrawn last month | Charged a late fee as a result of the missed withdrawal | Autopay settings still show as active
policy_cited: 06 Fee Waiver and Goodwill Credit Authority, 'When a waiver is NOT appropriate' (transaction history confirms the fee was correctly charged; no waiver applicable)
draft_text:
Thank you for writing to us about your missed autopay withdrawal and the late fee that followed. We understand it's frustrating to see a charge when you believed autopay was working, so we reviewed your account carefully.

Here is what we found on each point you raised:

1. The payment that wasn't withdrawn: You're right that the $100.00 installment due May 27 was not withdrawn, and our records show no payment received for it. Autopay did withdraw normally on March 27 and April 27. Our records show autopay was turned off through the mobile app on May 9, which was before the May 27 due date, so there was no active autopay instruction on that date.

2. The late fee: A $25.00 late fee was applied on June 1 because the May 27 installment was not received. Because the payment wasn't withdrawn and no other payment was received, our records show the fee was charged correctly, so we are not able to waive it.

3. Autopay showing as active: We don't have your screenshot on file, and it doesn't match what our records show for your account, which is that autopay was turned off on May 9. If you send us the screenshot, we'll review it, including the date it was taken. If you don't recognize the May 9 change, please tell us right away so we can look into it.

If you have anything else you'd like us to consider, you can send it at any time by replying to this message or calling the number on your account, and we will review it. You are also free to raise this through any other channel you choose.

narrative: My account is showing as 60 days past due on my credit report, but I have never missed a payment on this account. My bank statements show every payment was made on time for the past 18 months.
extracted_allegations: Account is showing as 60 days past due on credit report | Customer states they have never missed a payment on this account | Bank statements show every payment was made on time for the past 18 months
policy_cited: 04 Credit Reporting Disputes (FCRA): Requirements (30/45-day investigation timeline, consumer statement of dispute), What an analyst or agent may say, and Remedy authority (no correction initiated because the internal payment record supports what was reported). Policy 10 (Prohibited Language) and Policy 11 (Response Tone and Format) also applied.
draft_text:
We understand how stressful it is to see your account reported as 60 days past due when you believe every payment was made on time. We reviewed your account's payment records for this.

Your account was reported to the credit bureaus as 60 days past due on April 20, 2026. That report is in our records.

You also told us you have never missed a payment. Our payment log shows your $140.00 installments were received on January 18 and February 18, 2026. It shows no payment received for the installments due March 18 and April 18, 2026. A $280.00 payment on May 18 covered two installments, and a $140.00 payment arrived on June 18. Your account is now current. The 60-day status matches the two installments our log shows as not received.

You mentioned your bank statements show on-time payments for the past 18 months. We don't have those statements on file, and our review was based on our own payment log. Because that log shows the March and April installments as not received, we have not made a correction to what was reported. We would like to look at your statements. If they show payments made on or around March 18 and April 18 to this account, please send them and we will review them. You can send anything else you think is relevant at any time, and we will review it as well.

Our investigation of a credit reporting dispute is completed within 30 days. That can extend to 45 days if you send us additional information during that time. We can only speak for what we report. We can't say when a credit bureau will update its records. If you are not satisfied with the outcome, you can ask for a statement of your dispute to be included in your credit file.

You can reply to this message or call us at the number on your account. Case reference: 23623033.

The fees adding up: Our records show a $15 weekly extension fee was assessed on June 5, June 12, June 19, June 26, July 3 and July 10. That is six fees totalling $90, and your account is currently past due.

It would help to hear more about your situation, including the nature of your medical emergency in your own words and the payment amount you could manage right now. You don't need to send documentation at this stage. You can reply to this message or call us at the number on your account at any time, and anything you send will be reviewed.
